name: MonarchRecoveryCodes
title: RecoveryCodes
wrapsNative: LazyVGrid of monospaced Text; MonarchCopyButton, ShareLink with a Transferable text file, confirmationDialog, Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox)
summary: One-time recovery codes in a monospaced grid, with copy, save or share, an optional show and hide button, generate new codes behind a confirmation, and an acknowledgement for setup flows.
whenToUse: When two-step verification is set up or reviewed, to give the person their backup codes and make sure they saved them.
whenNotToUse: Not for a single secret such as an API key (use MonarchCopyButton beside the value) and not for one-time passcodes the person types (use MonarchOtpPinInput).
api: init(_ codes: [MonarchRecoveryCode], heading: String? = nil, fileName: String = "recovery-codes.txt", startsRevealed: Bool = true, showsRevealToggle: Bool? = nil, labels: MonarchRecoveryCodesLabels = MonarchRecoveryCodesLabels(), onRegenerate: (@MainActor () async -> Void)? = nil, onAcknowledge: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
struct MonarchRecoveryCode: ExpressibleByStringLiteral { init(_ code: String, isUsed: Bool = false) }

options.name: codes
options.description: The codes, as values or string literals. Used codes are struck through and not copied or saved.

options.name: heading
options.description: A first line for the copied and saved text, such as the product and account, followed by a blank line.

options.name: fileName
options.description: The name of the text file offered in the share sheet.

options.name: startsRevealed
options.description: Whether the codes are visible at first.

options.name: showsRevealToggle
options.description: Whether the show and hide button is shown. By default when the codes start hidden.

options.name: onRegenerate
options.description: Replaces the codes after a destructive confirmation; pass the new codes back through codes. The button shows progress until it returns, then the new codes are shown and announced. No button without it.

options.name: onAcknowledge
options.description: Runs when the person ticks "I have saved my recovery codes" and presses Continue. Neither is shown without it.

states.name: used codes
states.description: Struck through in the subtle text colour, with "8 of 10 codes left" above the grid.

states.name: hidden
states.description: A lock and a hint replace the grid until "Show codes" is pressed.

states.name: regenerating
states.description: The regenerate button shows a progress indicator.

states.name: acknowledgement missing
states.description: Pressing Continue without the checkbox shows an error with an icon in the danger strong colour, and announces it.

appearance: Codes sit on a panel with the subtle background and subtle border roles, in the code type role. Buttons are Monarch buttons: ghost for show and hide, secondary for copy and save, danger for regenerate, primary for Continue. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web's Download becomes "Save or share": a ShareLink with a plain-text file, from which the person can save to Files, a password manager or another app. The web's confirm dialog is the system confirmationDialog. Revealed state is internal (startsRevealed) rather than controlled. The web's formatRecoveryCodes helper is the heading parameter; a fully custom format is not offered. Several closures are optional (onRegenerate, onAcknowledge). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onRegenerate.
accessibility: The grid is a container named "Recovery codes".
Each code is spelled out character by character by VoiceOver.
A used code has the value "Used", so its state does not depend on the strike-through.
All actions are standard buttons with 44-point touch targets; the acknowledgement is a standard Toggle with the Monarch checkbox style.
New codes are announced after regenerating.
A missing acknowledgement is shown with an icon and text and announced.
edgeCases: The grid has as many columns as fit at 112 points each, scaled with Dynamic Type, so the largest text sizes show one column.
A new set of codes clears the acknowledgement; marking a code used does not.
The codes can be selected as text for manual copying.

examples.title: Settings, hidden at first
examples.code:
MonarchRecoveryCodes(
    ["4f7k-2m9q", MonarchRecoveryCode("8d3r-6t1w", isUsed: true), "7n4h-3j8k"],
    startsRevealed: false
)
